definitions.explanation: The practice of tasting and evaluating different types of sake, often done professionally to assess quality or recreationally to appreciate varieties.

examples.japanese: {酒蔵|さかぐら}で{利|き}き{酒|ざけ}をした。
examples.english: I did a sake tasting at a brewery.

examples.japanese: {利|き}き{酒|ざけ}セットを{注文|ちゅうもん}した。
examples.english: I ordered a sake tasting set.

examples.japanese: {利|き}き{酒|ざけ}で{銘柄|めいがら}を{当|あ}てる。
examples.english: I identify the brand through sake tasting.

examples.japanese: {日本酒|にほんしゅ}の{利|き}き{酒|ざけ}イベントに{参加|さんか}した。
examples.english: I participated in a sake tasting event.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{利|き}く (to taste/distinguish) + {酒|さけ} (sake/alcohol) → {酒|ざけ} (rendaku)

ALSO WRITTEN:
{利|き}き{酒|ざけ} is sometimes written as {唎酒|ききざけ} using a specialized kanji for tasting.

RELATED VOCABULARY:
- {利|き}き{酒師|ざけし}: sake sommelier
- {酒蔵|さかぐら}: sake brewery
- {銘柄|めいがら}: brand (of sake)
- {日本酒|にほんしゅ}: Japanese sake
- {地酒|じざけ}: local sake

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {利|き}き{酒|ざけ}をする: do sake tasting
- {利|き}き{酒|ざけ}セット: sake tasting set (flight)
- {利|き}き{酒|ざけ}イベント: sake tasting event
- {利|き}き{酒|ざけ}{大会|たいかい}: sake tasting competition

CULTURAL NOTE:
Sake tasting is a popular activity at Japanese breweries ({酒蔵|さかぐら}) and sake festivals. Many regions have their own specialty {地酒|じざけ} (local sake), and tasting tours are a form of regional tourism.
